research_problem: GraphQL queries can be exponentially costly; providers lack a cheap, accurate, backend-agnostic way to estimate query cost (83% of 30 public APIs document no query analysis)
technical_approach: Formal GraphQL semantics; pagination-aware configuration (limit arguments, default limits, weights, regex); linear-time static analyses computing provable upper bounds for resolve complexity and type complexity
primary_contribution: First provably correct static GraphQL query cost analysis plus first GraphQL query-response corpus
dataset_benchmark: 10,000 generated query-response pairs from GitHub and Yelp GraphQL APIs (Apr 2019-Mar 2020)
evaluation_metrics: Under/over-estimation rates, median and 90th-percentile error, runtime (ms)
baselines: Three open-source static libraries (libA, libB, libC); GitHub and Yelp closed analyses (qualitative)
key_findings: No under-estimation; 84% of GitHub type predictions over-estimate <50%; median error 19% vs libA 634%; libB/libC under-estimate ~64%; median 3.0 ms per query; GitHub DoS vector disclosed and patched; Yelp limit bug confirmed; shipped in IBM API Connect/DataPower v10
author_limitations: Configuration errors and query realism (random, bounded queries); depends on resolvers enforcing limits; configuration burden; mutation type complexity and hybrid static/dynamic left to future work; prototype not shareable
analyst_limitations: W1,0 weights never correlated with real server cost; only two large commercial APIs; synthetic corpus; closed prototype; Table 2 layout lost in conversion; modern attack vectors (batching, aliases) not considered
reproducibility: Zenodo corpus, generator and library configs; analysis prototype withheld
suggested_extensions: Hybrid learned cost models; automatic configuration inference from schema/LLM; fuzzing for resolver limit violations; cost-aware GraphQL test generation; mutation/subscription cost; REST/LLM-agent cost bounds
evidence_location: Motivation p.2; analysis p.5-6; corpus p.7; RQ2-4 p.7-8 Table 2; RQ5 p.9; disclosures p.10; threats p.11
integrity: Formulas partly garbled; heat-map axes scattered; Table 2 columns unrecoverable without PDF
